title: E2E streaming fanout throttling experimentation and mitigation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-08 we observed a multi-tenant streaming outage where a subset of streaming sessions experienced truncated output, partial-token emission, and frequent reconnect loops. Impact window ~18m; affected ~3% of streaming requests across two regions. Immediate mitigation was rate-limiting fanout at the edge and rolling back a slab throttle config change. Root cause analysis points to a regression in the fanout scheduler introduced as part of runtime-1.20 (fanout prioritization + aggressive slab_throttle tuning) combined with an unhandled race between fanout reference counting and token commit paths that caused lost downstream backpressure signals and KV-cache divergence for stalled sessions.
updates: 2026-02-08 - 14:27 UTC: Incident detected via streaming-error-rate alert (grafana/streaming). Pager duty routed to oncall; started mitigation runbook.
2026-02-08 - 14:32 UTC: Temporary mitigation: apply conservative fanout cap at edge (edge-config v2) to limit per-session parallelism. Error rate fell within 6 minutes.
2026-02-08 - 15:05 UTC: Rolled back slab_throttle change made in runtime-1.20-hotfix; monitoring shows queue saturation cleared.
2026-02-09 - 09:00 UTC: Post-incident triage concluded; assigned follow-up ENG-55112 to develop robust throttling experiments and telemetry to prevent recurrence.
2026-02-18 - 17:10 UTC: Prototype throttling harness merged to staging (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/5471). Load test results attached to Confluence.
2026-03-01 - 11:45 UTC: Observability work in progress: added fanout request traces and slab-queue histograms to streaming dashboard (https://grafana.redwood.net/d/streaming/fanout).
2026-03-04 - 16:22 UTC: Design review completed for deterministic fanout backpressure policy; awaiting engineering estimates for rollout gating.
2026-03-05 - 09:05 UTC: Added automated e2e fanout stress tests to CI; first run shows reduced partial-token incidence under synthetic workload.
action_items: AI-1: Implement deterministic fanout throttling policy that bounds per-session parallelism and enforces fair share across tenants (owner: Miguel; estimate 3s).
AI-2: Add end-to-end load tests that simulate high-fanout sessions with mixed-length prompts and KV-cache churn; integrate into CI with staged thresholds (owner: SRE team; estimate 5s).

AI-3: Instrument fanout scheduler to emit per-slab queue depth, enqueue latency, and reference-count events; add Grafana panels and alerts for sustained queue growth (owner: Observability; estimate 2s).

AI-4: Patch race in token-commit path to ensure backpressure signals cannot be lost when fanout refcount transitions from N to 0 (owner: Miguel; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/5471).
AI-5: Reconcile KV-cache invalidation window for stalled sessions and implement a safe replay/repair workflow for partial-token sessions (owner: Runtime; estimate 4s).
AI-6: Create customer-facing incident summary and targeted outreach for top affected tenants; coordinate with CS for follow-ups (owner: Support; due 2026-03-10).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic fanout throttling deployed to canary with no regression in latency P95 for single-session workloads.
E2E stress tests reproducibly demonstrate <0.05% partial-token rate at 3x production fanout levels.
Grafana alerts trigger before slab queue depth reaches pre-incident saturation levels and produce actionable runbook steps.
KV-cache repair path validated in staging with end-to-end reproduction and recorded recovery run.
Customer outreach completed for all tenants with >0.5% error exposure during the incident window.
notes: Related context: this incident exposed a brittle interaction between recent performance optimizations (runtime-1.20) and opportunistic config tuning. Avoid simultaneous config tuning and scheduler changes in the same release window.
Follow-on proposal: introduce a lightweight canary that exercises fanout-heavy sessions for every runtime change touching scheduler or slab_throttle.

PRs / artifacts: Runtime fix PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/5471; Confluence postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-55112+postmortem; Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/streaming/fanout
